articles.title: ESPHome keeps long-term sensor averages through a restart
articles.dek: A new sensor preserves a smoothed reading instead of starting again with the next measurement.
body: ESPHome adds a sensor that preserves a running average across device restarts. Makers smoothing a reading over hours, such as outdoor temperature, can keep that accumulated picture instead of rebuilding it from the first measurement after a reboot.

Clyde Stubbs supplies a choice between a fixed weight for each reading and an average that accounts for the time between readings. A further option suits sensors that publish only when their value changes. Saving and restoring the average is enabled by default, with an action to reset it. J. Nick Koston reviewed the component and its guide.

pullRequests.title: [exponential_moving_average] Add EMA preserved across reboots
[exponential_moving_average] Document new ema sensor

articles.title: Sendspin gives device makers a practical implementation handbook
articles.dek: Separate client and server guides explain pairing, playback and the experience people should expect.
body: Device makers and application developers gain a step-by-step handbook for building Sendspin products. It expands the former single-page guide into separate paths for clients that receive audio and servers that coordinate playback, with worked examples and an ESPHome starting point.

Marcel van der Veldt covers pairing choices for different hardware, encryption, timing, volume control and the screens a server should present. A single-page view can be printed to PDF. The handbook explains the protocol rather than replacing its specification, which remains the authority for its rules. Paulus Schoutsen reviewed the work.

pullRequests.title: Expand the implementation guide into a multi-chapter handbook

articles.title: Apple Watch sends Assist audio while you speak
articles.dek: Speech recognition can end the recording automatically, with tap and hold controls still available.
body: Home Assistant’s Apple Watch assistant sends audio to the iPhone while the wearer is speaking, instead of waiting for a finished recording. The recording can stop when Home Assistant’s speech pipeline or the iPhone’s local recognition detects the end of speech.

Bruno Pantaleão Gonçalves also restores a choice of tapping to start and send a request or holding and releasing to send it. An iPhone without streaming support still receives the completed recording through the existing route.

pullRequests.title: Stream Apple Watch Assist audio while recording
Allow tap or hold to talk in Apple Watch Assist

articles.title: ESPHome corrects microphone noise that keeps voice requests open
articles.dek: An M5Stack voice device’s audio-chip clock setting could prevent Home Assistant from recognizing the end of speech.
body: ESPHome corrects an audio-chip clock setting linked to high microphone noise on the M5Stack Atom EchoS3R. That noise could keep Home Assistant from recognizing when someone had finished speaking. The change makes the ES8311 chip’s clock multiplier match its configured value.

The issue report cited by the contributor found that correcting the setting lowered idle noise enough for Home Assistant to detect the end of speech. abderrahmen bejaoui makes his first contribution to ESPHome with the correction.

pullRequests.title: [es8311] Encode the REG02 MCLK pre-multiplier instead of writing the factor

articles.title: Music Assistant plays complete ORF catch-up broadcasts
articles.dek: Multi-part shows no longer stop at their first segment, and seeking reaches the requested point promptly.
body: Music Assistant plays all the audio segments in ORF Radiothek catch-up broadcasts instead of stopping after the first. In contributor DButter’s test, an Ö3 show containing five and a half hours of audio had previously stopped after 23 minutes; the corrected connection played all 13 segments.

Seeking skips directly to the requested segment and position. In the contributor’s live test, a jump to five hours and five minutes into the show returned valid audio within 0.15 seconds. Episode lists gain chronological ordering, and one failed day no longer hides every older day. OzGav reviewed the work.

pullRequests.title: ORF Radiothek: fix catch-up order, missing days and split broadcasts

articles.title: Home Assistant connects to Sofar inverters through serial ports
articles.dek: A wired RS485 link or an ESPHome serial proxy joins the existing network connection.
body: Sofar inverter owners gain a serial connection option in Home Assistant, including local serial ports and ports shared over the network by an ESPHome proxy. Setup detects the inverter model from its serial number, extending the existing Modbus network connection to inverters reached through their RS485 terminals.

Contributor darkrain-nl tested the connection on a real inverter through an ESPHome serial proxy. Existing network connections keep their current type; changing an existing connection between serial and network is separate work.

pullRequests.title: Add serial connection support to the Sofar integration

articles.title: ESPHome installs LN882H firmware from the browser
articles.dek: Makers gain a USB serial installation path for another chip family.
body: ESPHome Device Builder adds browser-based firmware installation for Lightning LN882H boards through a USB serial adapter. J. Nick Koston tested a generic board using the manual boot guide; it then started ESPHome and joined the network. This extends the browser installation path reported for Beken boards on October 1 to another chip family.

The installer guides makers through holding the boot pin low when a board cannot enter installation mode automatically. Serial logs normally use a different connection; a companion firmware correction lets the logger use the installation port without crashing the device at startup.

Read LN882H logs over Web Serial and add the LN882H to web.esphome.io

articles.title: Music Assistant restores iPhone lock-screen playback controls
articles.dek: Music lowers its volume for directions while podcasts and audiobooks pause and resume.
body: Music Assistant’s iPhone app restores its presence on the lock screen and media player widget while playing music. An earlier adjustment for spoken interruptions had inadvertently removed it. Music lowers its volume during Maps or Siri announcements; podcasts and audiobooks pause, then resume afterward.

David Bishop also prevents opening the app while playback is paused from making those controls disappear. Another app taking exclusive control of audio can still displace them. Andrii Mitnovych reviewed the correction.

pullRequests.title: Restore lock screen Now Playing for music on iOS

articles.title: ESPHome keeps LN882H devices running when Wi-Fi disappears
articles.dek: Two corrections prevent a failed scan or a restarted fallback network from resetting the chip.
body: ESPHome corrects two ways an LN882H device could repeatedly restart after losing Wi-Fi. A scan finding no networks could reset the chip about ten seconds later; starting its fallback access point for a second time could also trigger a reset.
J. Nick Koston tested both corrections with an LN882H kept off its network. Empty scans and repeated fallback-network starts then ran without resetting the board. Jesse Hills reviewed the work.

pullRequests.title: [libretiny] Keep a scan that finds no networks from resetting the LN882x
[wifi] Keep a second fallback AP start from resetting the LN882x

articles.title: Matter.js removes settings a device no longer supports
articles.dek: Firmware updates could leave obsolete values visible through repeated restarts.
body: Controllers built with Matter.js stop retaining settings that a device has removed in a firmware update. One reported case left an old light transition-time value visible even after restarting the server and reading the device again; attempts to change it did nothing.

Ingo Fischer makes the controller check saved settings against those the device still supports and request a fresh reading when its stored information needs correcting. Values the device still reports are retained.

pullRequests.title: fix(node): drop cached values of attributes the AttributeList omits

articles.title: ESPHome controls Home Assistant number helpers
articles.dek: Commands that silently did nothing use the helper’s correct action.
body: ESPHome fixes control of Home Assistant number helpers, such as a helper holding a target temperature. The connection previously used an action that only worked with ordinary number entities, so changing a helper through it did nothing.
Jesse Hills selects the helper’s matching action and rejects unsupported entity types during configuration. J. Nick Koston reviewed the correction.

pullRequests.title: [homeassistant] Use input_number.set_value for input_number entities

articles.title: ESPHome accepts valid settings for USB-connected heat meters
articles.dek: A configuration check rejected Kamstrup connections even when their serial settings were correct.
body: ESPHome stops rejecting correctly configured USB serial connections for equipment such as Kamstrup heat meters. A meter using two stop bits could fail validation even when its USB infrared head was already configured for exactly that setting.

Max Slotov also corrects false parity-mismatch reports for USB channels. The settings sent to the adapter stay the same; the change fixes how ESPHome checks them. Clyde Stubbs reviewed the correction.

pullRequests.title: [uart] Validate parity and stop bits correctly

articles.title: Fumis low-fuel alerts reach Home Assistant automations directly
articles.dek: A dedicated trigger works even with the pellet stove’s alert sensor disabled.
body: Fumis pellet-stove owners gain a dedicated Home Assistant trigger for building low-fuel notifications or other automations. It watches the selected stoves directly, so the alert sensor can remain disabled and there is no need to identify which sensor carries the warning.

Franck Nijhof also prevents a temporary loss of connection or another stove alert from being mistaken for a fresh low-fuel warning. After an integration reload, the first update establishes the starting state instead of firing the automation.

pullRequests.title: Add fuel became low trigger to Fumis integration

articles.title: Home Assistant gets notifications through to silent LaMetric displays
articles.dek: Soundless devices stop rejecting messages; a companion guide explains kiosk-mode restrictions.
body: Home Assistant leaves sound out of notifications sent to LaMetric devices without audio, such as SKY. These devices could reject the whole message when message, chart or legacy notification actions included a sound; the correction keeps the visual notification.

Franck Nijhof also explains a separate restriction for kiosk mode: only critical-priority notifications are accepted. The standard notification entity always sends informational priority, so owners need the message or legacy notification action to choose critical priority. He verified that behavior on a LaMetric TIME.
